turns.text: Hey Lloyd, I'm running into some weird errors with my inference server today. It started crashing right after I pulled the latest updates.
Hi Alan. Sorry to hear that. Did you check the logs for any specific error codes? Sometimes library updates can break compatibility.
Yeah, it looks like a platform mismatch. I realized that CPU inference setups may be affected by vLLM's XPU platform changes. That's probably why it's failing.
Ah, that makes sense. vLLM updates can sometimes have unexpected side effects on non-GPU backends if not carefully managed. You might need to pin the version.
I'll try that. By the way, do you want to grab dinner later? I'm thinking about that new Thai place on 5th.
Thai sounds great. Is that the one with the spicy curries?
Yes, that's the one. Let me know if you're free around 7 PM.
Lloyd, I've been doing some benchmarking on the new server rack. The scaling isn't as linear as I hoped.
That's common with high-core-count systems. Did you monitor the memory bandwidth utilization?
I did. It turns out that beyond 8-16 cores, additional cores provide diminishing returns as memory bandwidth saturates. So adding more cores won't help much.
Good catch. It's better to focus on optimizing the memory subsystem or using fewer, faster cores in that case.
Exactly. I'm going to stick with the 16-core configuration for now. Oh, did you see the weather forecast for next week?
I haven't checked recently. Is it looking rainy?
Looks like heavy rain on Tuesday and Wednesday. I'll need to bring an umbrella.
